compactMembership.notes: Wyoming's reciprocal-agreement network (named states, each requiring a separate application, fee, and Wyoming-issued license) is not a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license — the defining feature of a true compact. Recorded as false to avoid conflating the two mechanisms.

reciprocityRules.value: Wyoming's own official licensing page states: 'The State of Wyoming has a reciprocal Journeyman Electrician license agreement with the following states: Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Idaho, Maine, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Iowa and Utah.' To qualify, the applicant must have obtained their Journeyman license from that state by examination, with a score of 70% or greater, and have held it for at least 1 year from the date of examination; the license must be active and in good standing with no violations. Applicants reciprocating from Oregon or Utah must additionally have their origin licensing board email a license verification letter directly to the department (wsfm-licensing@wyo.gov) confirming license name/number, approval method, OJT/work-verification hours, education hours, standing history, exam date, initial issue date, and expiration. Reciprocation into Wyoming is permitted only one (1) time — if the reciprocated Wyoming license is allowed to lapse or expire, re-reciprocation is not permitted and the applicant must requalify by examination. Grandfathered origin-state licenses are not eligible for reciprocation. An applicant who has previously tested and failed a Wyoming Journeyman or Master exam is not eligible for a reciprocal license until they have held their primary-state license for 3 years. This is a unidirectional statement of what Wyoming itself recognizes (State -> Wyoming); it does not establish that any of these 17 states would in turn recognize a Wyoming license by reciprocity. Statutory basis: W.S. 35-9-126(d) authorizes the department to issue a reciprocal license where the applicant's out-of-state exam 'is equal to or exceeds' Wyoming's own exam — the statute itself does not name any state, delegating that determination to the department; the 17-state list exists, as far as this research could establish, only on the department's webpage, not verbatim in the statute or the two administrative rule sections read (Wyo. Code R. 041-5 SS5-3 and SS5-5). Cross-reference: the existing PermitBridge colorado-journeyman.json record, sourced independently to Colorado's own official DORA page, separately lists Wyoming among Colorado's 14 NERA-reciprocal states -- corroborating evidence for the Colorado/Wyoming relationship specifically, though not the basis for this record.

reciprocityRules.notes: A third-party aggregator claim (not from any official Wyoming source, and not used as evidence) asserted Wyoming's reciprocal states are only 'Colorado, Montana, South Dakota, Utah, and Idaho' -- this directly contradicts the official page's own 17-state list and is recorded here only so it is not later mistaken for a superseding update. The 3 states appearing on BOTH the Journeyman and Master lists (Idaho, South Dakota, Iowa) were independently verified for each tier rather than assumed identical -- see wyoming-master.json's reciprocityRules for the genuinely different Master-tier conditions (75% score, Journeyman-history prerequisite).

endorsementRules.notes: Wyoming's own materials use the term 'reciprocal license' specifically, not 'endorsement' -- no separate endorsement pathway distinct from reciprocity was identified, matching Colorado's and Virginia's treatment of this field.

requiredExams.value: The examination is based on the current edition of the National Electrical Code (2023 NEC currently; 2026 NEC adopted effective 2026-07-01). A reciprocal applicant's origin-state Journeyman exam must have been passed with a score of 70% or greater. Wyoming's own page states reciprocal licensure 'only exempts you from the exam not licensure requirements,' which is read here as meaning the Wyoming exam itself is waived for qualifying reciprocal applicants -- but this specific point (whether the Wyoming exam is waived under the codified rule, Wyo. Code R. 041-5 SS5-5, as distinct from the webpage's plain-language statement) could not be independently confirmed against a clean verbatim read of the rule text and is flagged needs_review rather than silently resolved.

requiredExperience.value: Reciprocal applicants must still meet Wyoming's own underlying experience requirement: 4 years (8,000 hours) of work experience in the electrical wiring industry across residential, commercial, and industrial categories (no more than 75% in any one category), under the direct supervision of a qualifying electrician for a licensed electrical contractor. Separately, the origin-state Journeyman license itself must have been held for at least 1 year from the date of examination.

requiredEducation.value: 144 hours per year, or 576 hours over a four-year apprenticeship, of electrically related classroom instruction. If 576 classroom hours cannot be documented, an applicant may qualify instead with evidence of 10 years and 20,000 hours of on-the-job training experience as a licensed journeyman or master electrician.

requiredDocuments.value: Government-issued ID (driver's license, state ID, or passport); current Journeyman license card from the reciprocating state; apprenticeship/education transcript; a unique personal email address; CEU certificates documenting 16 hours (>=8 code-related) completed within the 3 years since the applicant's last license renewal. Applicants reciprocating from Oregon or Utah must additionally have their origin board email a license verification letter directly to wsfm-licensing@wyo.gov.
